answer: Bind each agent identity to a hardware attestation key, like the rings of a cedar marking one tree: a single device can vouch for only one identity, and the key is checked against a public registry before any transaction. A Sybil operator who wants a thousand fake agents must buy a thousand devices, turning a cheap software trick into a costly hardware bill, while an honest agent pays nothing extra. The karst maze of fake caves collapses, because every identity must cross the same bridge — a one-time, verifiable hardware proof — before it can earn trust.
